meta.titre: Multipurpose River Projects: benefits, problems and dam sites
meta.sous_theme: Purposes, advantages, problems and examples of river development schemes

sections.contenu_markdown: Every year the Benue River in the north of Cameroon rises with the rains and falls in the dry season. Farmers need water in the dry months, towns need electricity and villages fear floods. A single dam can help with all these needs at once, which is why governments build multipurpose projects. At the GCE, you can be asked to name the purposes of such a project, to explain its advantages and to discuss the problems it creates. The best answers give examples from Cameroon and from other countries.

items: A river basin is the area drained by a river and its tributaries.
Hydroelectric power is electricity produced by moving water.
A reservoir is an artificial lake kept behind a dam.

sections.titre: What a multipurpose river project does and what it costs
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Meaning
A **multipurpose river project** develops a river for several uses at the same time. Usually a dam is built across the river, and the water stored behind it forms a reservoir.

### Purposes and benefits
| Purpose | How it works | Benefit |
|---|---|---|
| Hydroelectric power | Water from the reservoir turns turbines | Electricity for homes, industries and sale |
| Irrigation | Water is sent through canals to fields | Farming in the dry season, higher yields |
| Flood control | The reservoir stores extra water in the rainy season | Protects farms and villages downstream |
| Water supply | Water is treated and piped | Drinking water for towns and industry |
| Fishing and tourism | The lake supports fish, boating and recreation | Food, jobs and income |
| Navigation | A steadier river level | Easier transport by boat |

### Problems (adverse effects)
- **People are displaced** from the land that the reservoir floods, and farmland, forest and wildlife habitats are lost.
- **Diseases** such as bilharzia and malaria can spread because still water favours snails and mosquitoes.
- **Silt** is trapped behind the dam. The reservoir slowly fills, and fertile silt no longer reaches the fields downstream.
- **Cost:** a dam needs very large investment, often financed by loans.
- **Flood risk:** a sudden release of water from a full reservoir, or a dam failure, can flood villages downstream.

### Examples
The Lagdo dam on the Benue River in northern Cameroon supplies electricity, water for irrigation and fish, and helps to control floods. The Edea and Song Loulou hydroelectric stations are on the Sanaga River. Outside Cameroon, the Aswan High Dam on the Nile in Egypt and the Tennessee Valley Authority in the United States are well-known schemes.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says state, name or explain the benefits of a project
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use one point per paragraph or per line: name the purpose, explain how the project achieves it, then give the result. Example: "Irrigation: water from the reservoir is carried by canals to the fields, so farmers can grow crops in the dry season and harvest more." A named example adds a mark.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks you to discuss, evaluate or give both sides
variantes.contenu_markdown: Pair every problem with a way of reducing it: fair compensation and new land for displaced families, health campaigns and clean water against disease, careful planning of the release of water, and planting trees on slopes to reduce silt. Finish with a short judgement on whether the benefits outweigh the costs.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks why a dam was built at a given place
variantes.contenu_markdown: A good site has a narrow valley with steep sides, so that a short dam can hold a deep reservoir; a strong rock foundation; a reliable river flow through the year from a large catchment area; few people living in the reservoir area; and a market for the electricity not too far away.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain three benefits and two problems of a multipurpose river project. (10 marks)

etapes.action: Choose three benefits that can be explained in a sentence each.
etapes.justification: Explain means giving the how, not only the name.

etapes.action: Write each benefit as name, mechanism, result.
etapes.justification: This structure gives marks for every part.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Power: water turns turbines, so electricity reaches homes and industries. Irrigation: canals carry water, so crops grow in the dry season. Flood control: the reservoir stores water, so farms downstream are protected.

etapes.action: Choose two problems and explain each with a cause and a consequence.
etapes.justification: A problem needs a reason, otherwise it is only a list.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Displacement: the reservoir floods villages, so families lose homes and farms. Disease: still water favours snails and mosquitoes, so bilharzia and malaria spread.

etapes.action: Add one named example and close with a short conclusion.
etapes.justification: A named example shows knowledge of the real world.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The Lagdo dam on the Benue River provides electricity and irrigation.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: A multipurpose project brings three main benefits. First, hydroelectric power: water from the reservoir turns turbines, so electricity is supplied to homes and industries. Second, irrigation: canals carry water to the fields, so crops can be grown in the dry season. Third, flood control: the reservoir stores extra water in the rainy season and protects farms downstream. There are also problems. People are displaced when the reservoir floods their villages and farms, and diseases such as bilharzia and malaria spread near the still water. The Lagdo dam on the Benue River shows both the benefits and the problems.

items.erreur_markdown: "A multipurpose project is built only to produce electricity."
items.pourquoi_faux: Electricity is one purpose. A multipurpose project serves several purposes at once, such as irrigation, flood control, water supply and fishing.
items.correction_markdown: Always name at least three purposes and explain each of them.

items.erreur_markdown: "The dam is useful because it is useful to farmers." with no further explanation.
items.pourquoi_faux: A statement without a mechanism earns no mark. The examiner wants to know how the dam helps.
items.correction_markdown: "The reservoir supplies canals that carry water to the fields, so farmers can grow crops during the dry season."

items.erreur_markdown: "Because silt is trapped behind the dam, the land downstream becomes more fertile."
items.pourquoi_faux: The reasoning is reversed. Fertile silt carried by floods enriches the land. When the dam holds it back, the land downstream receives less of it.
items.correction_markdown: Silt trapped behind the dam fills the reservoir and **reduces** the fertile silt reaching the fields downstream.

items.erreur_markdown: "The Lagdo dam is built on the Sanaga River."
items.pourquoi_faux: This is a wrong location. The Sanaga is the river of the Edea and Song Loulou stations.
items.correction_markdown: The Lagdo dam is on the **Benue River**, in northern Cameroon.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing "pollution" as the only problem of a dam.
items.pourquoi_faux: The word is vague and it is not clear what is polluted or how. Specific problems earn marks.
items.correction_markdown: Name the problem and explain it: displacement of villagers, loss of farmland and wildlife, spread of bilharzia and malaria, and silting of the reservoir.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) State four purposes of a multipurpose river project. (b) State one adverse effect.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Any four: hydroelectric power, irrigation, flood control, water supply, fishing, navigation, tourism. (b) Any one: displacement of people, loss of farmland and wildlife habitats, spread of waterborne diseases, silting of the reservoir, high cost, flooding after a sudden release of water.

items.enonce_markdown: Explain how a dam can reduce floods downstream, and why a sudden release of water from the reservoir can still cause floods.
items.solution_markdown: In the rainy season the river brings more water than usual. The reservoir stores the extra water, so the flow below the dam stays lower and fields and villages are protected. The water is then released slowly in the dry months. If the reservoir is already full and a large volume is suddenly released through the gates, the river below receives more water than its channel can hold, and it overflows onto the land. Award a mark for storing in the rainy season, a mark for controlled release, and marks for the cause of the sudden flood.

items.enonce_markdown: A district council plans a dam. The cost is 120 billion FCFA and the net income expected each year is 8 billion FCFA. About 2,000 families will lose their land. (a) Calculate how many years the net income will take to repay the cost. (b) Discuss whether the project should go ahead, giving two arguments for and two against.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $120 \div 8 = $ **15 years**.

(b) For: electricity and irrigation help industries and farms and create jobs; flood control protects people and their property. Against: 2,000 families lose their land and homes, so fair compensation and new land are needed; the cost is very high and repayment takes 15 years, during which diseases and silting may also cause costs. A good conclusion weighs both sides, for example: the project is worthwhile only if the families are properly resettled and the health risks are managed.

items_markdown: A multipurpose river project uses a dam and a reservoir to serve several purposes at once.
Main benefits: hydroelectric power, irrigation, flood control, water supply, fishing, navigation and tourism.
Main problems: displacement of people, loss of land and habitats, waterborne diseases, silting, high cost and flood risk after sudden releases.
Give examples: Lagdo (Benue River), Edea and Song Loulou (Sanaga River), the Aswan High Dam (Nile).
Explain every point with the mechanism and the result, and in a discussion weigh benefits against problems.
